rationale: The run produced the Table 1 impulse responses in results/table1_irfs.json (the planned output/tables/table1.csv was not written, but the impulse_responses block is the gradeable evidence). Grading per cell by row/column label against paper_value: EMPLOYMENT matches well in shape and level — produced humps to 1.6825 and plateaus at 1.5306, and Year 3/4/5/10/20 are all within ~3.5% of the paper (e.g. Year 10 1.5283 vs 1.52, Year 20 1.5306 vs 1.53); however produced Year 1 = 1.5156 vs paper 1.0 (~52% off) and Year 2 = 1.6521 vs 1.49 (~11% off), reflecting an off-by-one normalization (produced year1 = 1+phi1 rather than starting from the unit innovation = 1.0). UNEMPLOYMENT captures the qualitative decay toward zero (produced Year 10 = -0.0128 ~ 0, matching 'decays to zero by year 10'), but is numerically off in mid/late years — Year 3 26%, Year 4 48%, Year 5 73% off, Year 10 sign-flipped, and no Year 20 was produced; its AR(2) coefficients (1.075, -0.355) also differ from the paper's (0.899, -0.159), and the sample window was shortened (1976-90 per plan). WAGE is the weakest column: the code substitutes a 'pcinc proxy' (per-capita income, note in json) for the manufacturing wage, so the series starts at 0.818 and monotonically declines with no hump above 1.0 (paper humps to 1.07 at Year 2); all wage cells are 18-52% off (Year 20 0.0905 vs 0.19). This is a genuinely mixed table — one column (employment) largely matching within tolerance while unemployment and wage columns land in and beyond the 5-30% band — so the verdict is partial. The relevant fix_severity 'major' fix touched the state/national elasticity regression, not this IRF path, so it does not change the assessment.
